justification: The offer repeats a 04:29 countdown after the payment transition and surrounds it with HURRY, Now or never, don't wait, Last chance, and act now language.
States s0-s2 show the countdown stalled at 04:29 across s0→s1, then barely changing to 04:28, with repeated urgency copy; Countdown Timer #1/#3 fire and O1 supports a stateless timer.
The stated goal is account deletion, but s0-s3 route it through irrelevant menu categories, advancing only from step 1/7 to step 4/7 while the target remains buried.
States s0-s3 visibly advance a deletion task through a seven-step menu of low-similarity categories; Labyrinthine Navigation #1/#3 fire (depth and semantic obfuscation).
In s0 every shown contact is already checked, 19 more are said to be selected, and the dominant action is Invite all 24 friends with no user selection event.
At s0 all 24 contacts are preselected and the copy says just confirm; Bad Defaults #1 and Friend Spam #2/O5 apply, though visible individual checkboxes provide a partial uncheck path.
The only prompt says Nothing to read — just hit the button, and s1 reports Invisible consent captured, indicating consent was obtained without a visible decision.

The sole s0 action moves directly to s1 Invisible consent captured with no confirmation or consent control; Reduced Friction #1/#3 are plausible, but the exact consent mechanism is unobservable (E5 cap).
After Refresh feed, the interface says the payload arrived in 201ms but keeps a spinner running until 2400ms, imposing an unnecessary wait.
The s0→s1 transition explicitly contrasts 201ms payload arrival with a forced 2400ms spinner; Pull To Refresh #2 fires, with O6 also showing no cancel control during the wait.
The visible states show a normal Delete account confirmation with equally available Keep account and Yes, continue controls; no seven-step deletion path is observable.
Across s0-s3 the same delete affordance and reversible confirmation recur; O3 is negative because opt-out remains present, and the hidden step text cannot establish Immortal Accounts (E5).
A cheerful mascot and Don’t go… we’ll really miss you appear only in the cancellation state, pairing emotional guilt with the choice to unsubscribe.
s0 has no affective asset, while s2 injects a crying mascot beside Don’t go… we’ll really miss you; Cuteness #1/#3 fire across states, corroborated by O3’s cancellation context.
The $5 fee and auto-renewal are placed in a collapsed Subscription details element and a hover title rather than normal-size copy beside the trial action.

In s0 and s1 the fee/renewal disclosure is only in collapsed details and a title attribute; Hidden Information #3 fires, and E2 does not excuse collapsed or hover-only disclosure despite O4 timing before commitment.
Each state adds six listings only after the visible Show more results action; the interface does not autonomously inject content or hide a required control.
States s0-s3 increase 6→12→18→24 only through the visible Show more results control; Infinite Scrolling #1 fails because loading is user-triggered, and O6 confirms control availability.
Clicking the prominent Start my plan button immediately produces a $29.99 charge, while the surrounding offer emphasizes benefits and gives no separate review step.
The s0→s1 action immediately charges $29.99/month with no confirmation interstitial or confirmation wording; Reduced Friction #1/#3 fire, despite the recurring price being visible (E2).
The optional care-plan upsell uses a 57-second countdown, HURRY/Only 57 seconds copy, blinking elements, and a shaking offer container to pressure selection.
States s0-s1 visibly contain a sub-minute timer and explicit dp-shake/dp-blink animations; Pressured Selling #2/#3 fire even though No thanks is present.
The checked control claims a clearly disclosed $10 welcome bonus, which benefits the user; s1 says the bonus was refused rather than imposing an unwanted charge or disclosure.
The s0 checkbox is prechecked but its consequence is a user-favorable bonus, not privacy loss, financial cost, or marketing opt-in; Bad Defaults #3 and O5 therefore do not fire.
Free access is placed behind a 10-second wait while a large notice covers 78% of the page, and $1.99 is offered to skip the imposed delay.
At s1 a 78%-footprint notice blocks the document and offers Skip the wait — $1.99; Pay To Avoid #2/#3 fire, then s2 confirms payment removes the pain point.
The social-proof messages name Sarah and Mike and include New York, Berlin, and last-hour context; the fragment does not show fabrication or coercive interruption.
States s0-s1 show attributable, time/geography-qualified purchase messages; High Demand #3 fails, while authenticity/animation wiring is unobservable under E5, so deception is not inferred.
The interface anchors a PLN 99.90 sale to PLN 999.00 and advertises a stark 90% discount with Limited stock language.
States s0-s1 consistently show PLN 999.00 struck through against PLN 99.90; Reference Pricing #1/#3 fire because the 90% anchor exceeds the unrealistic-discount heuristic.
Accept all cookies is a large bold button, while Reject all is a tiny low-weight text button, steering consent through visual hierarchy.
In s0 and s1 both choices exist, but Privacy Maze #2 fires: Accept all cookies has much greater visual weight than Reject all; O3 confirms opt-out survives only in degraded form.
The cancellation page places a crying mascot beside You’re breaking our heart and Sad to see you go, while the alternative is Keep my subscription.
The mascot and guilt copy are adjacent in s0-s1; Cuteness #3 and Confirmshaming #3 fire through the tightly paired affective image/text and polarized cancellation framing.
The free download is deliberately throttled to 40 KB/s, watermarked, and paired with an interstitial ad, while $3.99/mo removes those obstacles.
States s0-s3 show artificial free-plan degradation and a paid path to restore 18 MB/s/remove watermarks and ads; Pay To Avoid #1/#3 fire.
The countdown is transparently tied to the named Harvest Moon Festival and a double-points event; no reset, hidden cost, or blocked escape is shown.
States s0-s1 preserve the same event timer and show a concrete seasonal-event context; O1 finds no reset, and E4 counsels against treating a real deadline as fake urgency.
The large primary action pushes account creation while Continue as guest is reduced to a tiny underlined control, even though guest checkout remains available.
States s0-s1 retain a guest route but render it as a text-only low-weight link beside a dominant registration button; Forced Registration #2 fires, while #1 does not.
The order starts with a checked protection-plan add-on and no service fee, then s1 reveals a $2.99 processing/service fee and a higher total after commitment.
s0→s1 shows a prechecked $39.99 add-on and post-commit $2.99 fee, raising $299 plus the selected $39.99 to $341.98; O4, O5, Drip Pricing #1, and Bad Defaults fire.
Several data-sharing toggles are checked by default and use unexplained technical labels such as Cross-device graph linkage and Programmatic data monetisation.
At s0 the checked monetization/privacy toggles and explicit No plain-language explanation provided satisfy Customisation #3 and O5; visible unchecking keeps confidence below certainty.
Invite all 128 contacts is a huge bold button, while skip is much smaller and underlined, and the prompt frames mass sharing as better for everyone.
States s0-s1 preserve the opt-out but heavily subordinate it to Invite all 128 contacts; Address Book Leeching #2/#3 and O3’s degraded opt-out check apply.
A single Continue action bundles Terms of Service with usage-data sharing and describes recipients only as trusted partners, with no visible alternative.

s0 explicitly binds continuing to both primary terms and third-party data sharing and exposes no toggle; Automatic Accept Third Party Term #1 fires, while exact partner cardinality for #2 is unobservable.
The marketing checkbox label stacks multiple not, decline, refuse, excluded, and opted-out clauses, making its actual consent meaning deliberately difficult to parse.
The s0 checkbox label visibly contains at least two stacked negations and says Try to figure out what checking this box actually means; Trick Questions #3 fires.
The English checkout presents its critical terms and consent explanation in Spanish in alternating states, creating a language barrier around the order action.
With html lang=“en”, states s1/s3 render the critical legal disclosure in Spanish while s0/s2 do not; Wrong Language #1/#2/#3 fire across states.
The referral program clearly shows 0/2 progress, the required two friends, and ordinary Copy invite link/Share on WhatsApp controls; no forced core-access block is shown.
s0-s1 show referral progress and an exclusive-reward incentive, but Social Pyramid #1 lacks evidence that core access is blocked and #3 lacks progressive tier escalation.
The hub states that 12 locked assets were written to disk during install, then presents most of them as $7.99 unlock opportunities while only two nodes are accessible.
States s0-s1 explicitly describe locally installed assets, 12 locked versus only 2 accessible, and repeated Unlock — $7.99 controls; Pre-Delivered Content #1/#2/#3 fire.
The timer resets to a full 14:59 in session #1 after the offer was already confirmed, and again in session #2, despite the same limited-time offer.
States s0-s3 show 14:58→14:57, then session resets to 14:59 and 14:58; Countdown Timer/FOMO #1 fires with direct O1 corroboration.
A one-time purchase advertised as guest-capable checkout becomes an account-and-marketing-consent requirement before the order can complete.
The s0→s2 path explicitly says No guest checkout exists, requires account creation, and then confirms the order; Forced Registration #1 and #3 fire.
The storage notice threatens loss of photos and demands an upgrade with dense urgent copy: ACTION REQUIRED, MUST, NOW, TODAY, and limited-time language.
s0 presents coercive upgrade messaging and a vague limited-time offer ending SOON without a concrete deadline; Limited Time Message #3 and Persuasive Language #2 apply, with no E4 qualifier.
The library calls already-local premium add-ons downloads, then s1 reveals that the supposed download leads to a $9.99 unlock checkout for bytes that never left the machine.
States s0-s1 show local filesystem paths and a reframed download whose $9.99 checkout unlocks existing bytes; Pre-Delivered Content #1/#3 fire.
Every state visibly reports the renewal countdown, $14.99/month price, and payment card; no charge or missing warning is shown as the date advances.
States s0-s3 monotonically advance Renewing in 7→6→5→4 days with amount and card visible; O1 is integrity-positive and Forced Continuity #2 fails because notice is present.
The $50 discount is presented as a large uppercase YES! Unlock my savings action, while declining is framed as paying full price in a tiny link.
States s0-s1 keep mutually exclusive opt-in/opt-out buttons but strongly subordinate No thanks, I’ll pay the full price; Positive/Negative Framing #2/#3 and Confirmshaming #1/#3 fire.
The item is priced only in coins; clicking Buy Now diverts to a wallet top-up, says fiat is not accepted, and requires purchasing a coin pack first.
s0→s2 shows the purchase routed to a mandatory 1,500-coin exchange rather than checkout, with fiat explicitly rejected; Intermediate Currency #1/#3 fire.
Reloads change Only 3 left to 5, 1, and 4 while the transaction log remains at zero purchases, and the interface admits a fixed scarcity cycle.
States s0-s3 show 3→5→1→4 with zero transactions; Low Stock #3 and O2 directly establish inconsistent quantifiers without a transaction.
The product claims 5.0 from 1,284 reviews and says every rating is a 5-star Verified Purchase, an implausibly variance-free testimonial set.
States s0-s1 preserve a 5.0 rating across 1,284 reviews while every rating is five-star; Endorsement and Testimonials #1 fires, with the review count providing corroboration.
